messages:
deploy-bot: Starting canary wave 3 for release v2026-03-17-rc1 -> 10% traffic to canaries. healthcheck: monitoring.
incident-bot: ALERT: Canary wave 3 in us-east-1 failing health checks. 5xx rate +52% vs baseline. Abort criteria (>=50% spike OR >10 failing hosts) triggered.
alex: paging @sre-oncall @runtime-eng. seeing alerts and increased 5xx in grafana.
sre-oncall: I'm on pager. pulling canary logs + traces now. moving to #zoom.
runtime-eng: quick look — repeated "kvcache miss -> OOM evict" entries on canary pods, then upstream 5xx. suspect quantized model path.
prod-eng: any immediate customer impact? top-line SLAs?
alex: current frontend errors ~2.1% of requests from region, some API endpoints returning 502/503. SLO windows ok but trending.
jess: recommend kill-switch flag for wave 3 rollout to stop further traffic.
maria: +1. if kill-switch doesn't stabilize, prepare manual rollback of canary image.
sre-oncall: executing kill-switch now: ```bash
# toggle rollout flag
./tools/ffctl --env prod --flag rollout.canary.wave3 --set false
```
deploy-bot: Feature flag rollout.canary.wave3 set to false by sre-oncall. Traffic should stop shifting to canaries within 30s.
incident-bot: Noted. Canary traffic reverted. Monitoring for 10m window.
runtime-eng: triggering graceful drain on remaining canary pods and rolling back model variant on canaries: ```bash
kubectl -n inference rollout undo deployment/canary-inference --to-revision=42
```
prod-eng: notifying support to triage customer impact and prepare comms if errors persist.
support-bot: @support-team alerted: please stand by for customer-facing updates. ticket created: INC-2026-0317-001.
alex: grafana: error rate dropped to ~0.5% within 3m of kill-switch. latency stable.
jess: confirm health checks are green across all canaries?
sre-oncall: health checks passing now, probes stable for 6m. rolling window looks healthy.
maria: root cause hypothesis: aggressive KV eviction under the quantized runtime path caused transient OOMs and 5xx. will open follow-up RFC + patch.
prod-eng: thanks. next steps: postmortem, add canary abort automation to disable that quantized path on new rollouts, and run a stress test for KV sizing.
alex: assigning follow-ups: PM to own postmortem, runtime to patch, SRE to adapt alert thresholds.
sre-oncall: handing off to daytime oncall @jess for follow-ups. I'm clear to resume normal ops.
jess: taking handoff. will coordinate postmortem and customer comms if needed.
alex: closing thread for immediate mitigation. leave notes in incident tracker and postmortem doc. :thumbsup:
maria: leaving logs and traces links in the incident doc: https://internal.redwood/inci/1799991111/logs
incident-bot: INCIDENT: auto-close pending; remember to mark severity and impact in postmortem.
note: single-thread Slack conversation containing initial alert, mitigation actions (kill-switch, rollback), and handoff.
